context:
See the two Land Use Land Cover maps of Ichalkaranji city, Kolhapur district, given below and observe how changes have occurred in the city over the years. Map A) is for 2007 and map B) for 2017. Both are at a scale of 1:80,000 and were generated by the Maharashtra Remote Sensing Application Centre, Department of Planning, Government of Maharashtra.

The legend is:

| Colour | Land use / land cover class |
|---|---|
| Pale yellow | Agriculture |
| Olive green | Forest |
| Light pink (mauve) | Wasteland-Scrub |
| Blue | Waterbodies |
| Dark red | Built Up - Rural |
| Bright pink (magenta) | Built Up - Residential |
| Salmon | Built Up - Residential-Sparse |
| Navy blue | Built Up - Industrial |
| Purple | Built Up - Public/Semipublic |
| Dark green | Built Up - Recreation |
| Brown | Built Up - Mining/Quarry |
| Pale teal | Built Up - Open Space |

On both maps a blue line runs across the south-east corner, labelled PANCHAGANAGA RIVER, and a network of thin black lines crosses the map. The settlements named are Ichalkaranji, Rui, Chandur, Sajani, Korochi, Takawade, Ingali, Haroli, Jambhali, Nandani, Kondigre, Yadrav, Mangaonwadi, Gaon Bhag and Shahu Nagar, with two areas marked INDUSTRIAL ESTATE. Also labelled are a stadium, several colleges and gardens, a sports complex, a playground, temples, a bus stand, an S.T. depot, an RTO office, an MSEB power station, a water treatment plant and a sewrage treatment plant.

Between 2007 and 2017 the bright pink residential area of Ichalkaranji spreads outward in every direction, most of it over ground that was pale yellow agriculture or light pink wasteland-scrub on the earlier map. The navy blue industrial patches also grow, and a brown mining/quarry patch appears in the north-west.
stem: Enlist the colours used for showing land uses in the index.
